ila (sdk): fyi ran into a bizarre typing mismatch after converting the sample to native ESM + esbuild publishing. overloads behave differently in the shipped .d.ts vs local tsc output.
ila (sdk): small public API: 
```ts
export function openFile(id: string): Promise<string>
export function openFile(opts: { id: string; asBinary: true }): Promise<Uint8Array>
export function openFile(arg: any) { /* impl */ }
```
ila (sdk): consumers using bundlers get the first overload only. locally with tsc (node16 resolution) both show up.
ben (ts): that pattern trips up if you emit declarations under isolatedModules or moduleResolution: bundler. ts can collapse overloads when declaration emit lacks program-level info.
roxanne (devex): this impacted a getting-started tutorial where we show binary vs text results. users copying sample saw wrong types and got confused.
ben (ts): immediate options:
- add a dedicated tsc declaration step with moduleResolution: node16 and isolatedModules: false
- or flatten API to a discriminated generic to avoid relying on overload ordering
ila (sdk): i tried switching moduleResolution in a separate tsconfig for declarations and `tsc -p tsconfig.decls.json` fixed the published .d.ts order.
roxanne (devex): can you add a tiny CI job that compares tsc-emitted d.ts to the packaged d.ts and fails on diff? would prevent regressions.
ila (sdk): filed https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/2501 with repro and proposed CI step. tagging @roxanne @ben
ci-bot: created issue #2501 by ila (sdk) 917 : https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/2501
ben (ts): another note: be careful with `unknown` in conditional types in public signatures. some bundlers + emit combos widen inference. we documented a recommended pattern in internal-typing.md.
roxanne (devex): i'll update the sample app templates and onboarding guide with the recommended tsconfig snippet and a short note about ESM/ESBuild gotchas.
ila (sdk): thanks all, will land a quick patch in the sample to use the discriminated generic while CI change lands. :thumbsup:
